text:
maria.g: heads-up — I'm starting bring-up for a community model (Orion-7B-lite) that a partner wants us to benchmark. need a quant plan: int8 vs fp8 vs gguf export, and a quick checklist for calibration + evals. any workflow recs?

kevin.t: +1. suggest this order: 1) perf profile on fp16 baseline; 2) int8 symmetric/affine sweep; 3) fp8 candidate if hw supports; 4) gguf export tests for edge runtime. keep a small eval set for quick regressions.

lee: Agree with kevin. Add: run a small sensitivity sweep first (1000 prompts, mix of doc summarization / dialogs / code). Captures where int8 breaks.

maria.g: good. what metrics should we prioritize? perplexity? rouge/bertscore? latency & token cost?

philip: prioritize delta-quality + tail regressions. So: perplexity, BERTScore, and a simple token-drop detection (shortening hallucinations). Also track mean latency p50/p95 and tokens/sec.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created -> /deploys/checklists/orion-7b-lite-canary (auto).

kevin.t: for calibration: use 1) layerwise quant-aware pass; 2) per-channel stats; 3) optionally MSE vs KL calibration options. Keep calibration seed fixed.

maria.g: can someone paste a quick config snippet we can start with?

lee: sure. here's a minimal config we used previously:

```yaml
model: orion-7b-lite
precision: int8
calib:
  method: kl
  per_channel: true
  calib_dataset: "eval-mini-1k.jsonl"
  seed: 42
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  batching_policy: latency_sensitive
fallbacks:
  - fp16-hosted
  - fp32-dedicated
```

sara.k: quick note on gguf: it helps for distribution but double-check op compatibility (custom kernels might be dropped). If gguf export, run a functional smoke: 10 deterministic prompts, compare token-by-token.

maria.g: who can own the first pass (calibration + smoke)? i can do the eval harness but need someone with bench infra for the latency runs.

philip: I can run latency on the dedicated pool this afternoon. will run fp16 baseline + int8 calibrated. need the gguf after that.

kevin.t: let's gate canary rollout on two conditions: 1) quality delta <= 2% BERTScore drop vs fp16 on the mini set, and 2) p95 latency within 1.5x of fp16. if either fails, fallback to fp16 or try fp8.

maria.g: sounds good. timeline?

philip: can have baseline perf by EOD, int8 sweep by tomorrow morning if nobody blocks.

lee: I'll kick off a sensitivity sweep script now. Using these buckets: embedding prompts, long-doc summarization, code-completion. will post results in this thread.

sara.k: reminder: include a small safety eval (toxicity/escaping prompts). quant sometimes amplifies hallucination modes.

maria.g: adding that to the harness. also: please tag results with model hash + gguf/int8/fp8 label so we can track in the dashboard.

kevin.t: FYI — if int8 fails marginally, try hybrid strategy: KV-cache fp16, FFN int8. sometimes preserves LM head fidelity.

philip: noted. infra note: for fp8 tests we need a different AMI on dedicated nodes; might add 30–45m infra prep.

maria.g: OK. plan of action (short):
- run fp16 baseline (philip)
- sensitivity sweep (lee)
- int8 calibration sweep (maria/kevin)
- gguf export & functional smoke (sara)
- safety checks + BERTScore/regression analysis (maria)
- decide canary rollout by tomorrow afternoon (team)

kevin.t: also capture token-level cost estimate (tokens/sec * instance-cost) so we can show cost delta.

maria.g: great. i'll create a tiny tracking sheet + link it here when ready. thanks all :rocket:

ops-bot: Reminder: runbook for canary rollouts -> /runbooks/inference-canary.md

lee: posted first sweep results: ORION-7B-lite sensitivity CSV attached to the PR. TL;DR: int8 has 1.8% BERTScore drop on long docs, negligible on dialogs. attaching more details to the PR.

maria.g: awesome — will analyze and push the eval harness updates. if int8 looks acceptable on dialogs but not long docs, we can prioritize routing policy (dialog->int8, long-doc->fp16) as an interim.

philip: starting dedicated perf runs now. will share perf numbers in ~30m.

sara.k: i'll queue the gguf export after int8 looks stable.
